tests.name: example2
tests.description: Example 2 from problem statement: A = {13}

tests.name: example3
tests.description: Example 3 from problem statement: A = {0, 2, 7}

tests.name: n1_zero
tests.description: Singleton bound: A = {0}, minimum possible element

tests.name: n1_max_val
tests.description: Singleton bound: A = {2^30 - 1}, maximum possible element

tests.name: complement_pair
tests.description: Bitwise complement pair: A = {0, 2^30-1}. Each element is the 30-bit complement of the other.

tests.name: sparse_powers_of_two
tests.description: Sparse isolated bit boundaries: A = {2^0, 2^1, ..., 2^7}

tests.name: deep_collision
tests.description: Deep 30-bit collision: A = {2^30-2, 2^30-1}, differing only in bit 0. All 29 upper bits identical.

tests.name: midpoint_straddle
tests.description: Mask boundary: A = {2^29-1, 2^29}, elements on opposite sides of bit-29 midpoint.

tests.name: dense_consecutive
tests.description: Dense continuous sub-trie: A = {0, 1, ..., 7}, all 3-bit combinations.

tests.name: scattered_high_bits
tests.description: Pathological branching: A = {2^24, 2^25, ..., 2^29}, forcing many single-child Trie nodes.

tests.name: single_element_mid
tests.description: Small singleton: A = {42}

tests.name: bit29_boundary
tests.description: Three elements spanning the bit-29 boundary: {2^29-1, 2^29, 2^29+1}.

tests.name: sibling_saturation
tests.description: Sibling saturation at bit 1 and 0: A = {0,1,2,3}, all 2-bit combinations.

tests.name: large_spread
tests.description: Three widely spread elements with varying bit depths: {1, 10^6, 5*10^8}.

tests.name: all_powers_of_two_n30
tests.description: All 30 distinct powers of two: A = {2^0, 2^1, ..., 2^29}. Each element sets exactly one bit, forcing the Trie to branch at every level independently.

tests.name: stress_n400_random
tests.description: Stress: N=400 uniformly random distinct elements in [0, 2^30-1]. Validates general query efficiency.

tests.name: stress_n200_dense_low
tests.description: Stress: N=200 dense distinct elements in [0, 511] (dense low-bit subtrie, <=9 bit depth).

tests.name: stress_n400_high_half
tests.description: Stress: N=400 distinct elements all in [2^29, 2^30-1]. Tests bit-29 MSB split and mask boundary.

tests.name: adversarial_chain_trie
tests.description: Adversarial: 31 elements form a depth-30 chain in the XOR trie (chain_base=42, each 42^(1<<k) branches off at bit k). Element 42 sits at the bottom, reachable only by X=~42. 369 filler elements in [2^29, 2^29+370) pad to N=400. Random-query approaches cannot find element 42 (probability 2^{-30} per query).

tests.name: pitfall1_qx_vs_qx_xor_x
tests.description: Regression for Pitfall 1: Confusing Q(X) with Q(X) XOR X. A={42}, X=10 gives res=32. Wrong: insert 32. Correct: 32 XOR 10 = 42.

tests.name: pitfall4_early_exit_n2
tests.description: Regression for Pitfall 4: Early-exit efficiency. A={0,1}, both elements found quickly. Without early exit, many redundant probes would be issued.

tests.name: dense_consecutive_offset
tests.description: Dense consecutive sub-trie with non-zero base: A={100,101,...,107}. Tests complete sub-trie detection at low bits with offset.

tests.name: adversarial_chain_trie_fixed
tests.description: Adversarial: 31 chain elements (42 and 42 XOR 2^k for k=0..29) plus 370 fillers in [2^29, 2^29+369]. Total N=400. Element 42 is deep in the trie. Note: 42 XOR 2^29 = 536870954 falls in filler range, so it is not double-counted.

tests.name: mask_boundary_depth29
tests.description: Regression for Pitfall 3: Tests mask correctness at depth 29 (single-bit mask). A={2^29, 2^29+1} differ only in bit 0 but share bit 29=1.

tests.name: pitfall1_xor_back
tests.description: Targets Pitfall 1: forgetting to XOR the oracle result back with X. A={42}, querying X=10 returns 32, but the element is 32 XOR 10 = 42, not 32.

tests.name: pitfall3_mask_depth29
tests.description: Targets Pitfall 3: mask off-by-one at depth 29. A={2^29, 2^29+1}. At depth 29, correct mask is 2^29. An off-by-one mask would cover bits 28-29, potentially pruning valid branches.

tests.name: pitfall2_not_masking
tests.description: Targets Pitfall 2: bitwise NOT without masking. A={0, 3}. When probing prefix 0 at various depths, NOT(0) must be masked to stay in [0, 2^30).

tests.name: pitfall4_early_exit
tests.description: Targets Pitfall 4: missing early exit. A={0,1} are found quickly, but without early exit the DFS would issue many redundant queries across 30 depth levels.

tests.name: two_elements_far_apart
tests.description: Two elements with maximum Hamming distance in bit representations: A={0, 2^30-1}. Tests that the algorithm correctly explores both sides of every bit split.

tests.name: three_close_elements
tests.description: Three elements differing only in the lowest 2 bits: A={100, 101, 103}. Tests deep trie branching where upper 28 bits are identical.

tests.name: n400_dense_low_8bit
tests.description: N=256 elements packed densely in [0, 255] (all 8-bit values). Tests dense sub-trie exploration.

tests.name: deterministic_n400_consecutive
tests.description: Deterministic max-N test: N=400 consecutive integers {0,1,...,399}. Validates correctness and query count at the maximum constraint with a fully known expected answer.

tests.name: pitfall_xor_recovery_isolation
tests.description: Isolates Pitfall 1 (forgetting y = Q(X) XOR X): single element 42, bootstrap with X=0 returns 42, which must be XOR'd with 0 to get 42. A buggy solver that skips the XOR would still get this right, but element 999999999 at X=0 returns 999999999 which if not XOR'd with 0 is the same. So we test N=2 where Q(0)=999999999 XOR 0=999999999 gives first element, and the second element 500000000 requires proper XOR recovery from a non-zero X probe.

tests.name: pitfall_mask_boundary_depth29
tests.description: Isolates Pitfall 3 (mask off-by-one): Two elements differing only at bit 29 boundary. A = {0, 536870912}. If mask at depth 29 is wrong (covers 2 bits instead of 1), the bit-28 branch exploration is corrupted and element 0 may be missed.

tests.name: pitfall_early_exit_n2_close
tests.description: Isolates Pitfall 4 (missing inner early-exit): N=2 with A={0,1}. Both elements share 29 upper zero bits. Without early exit after finding both, the DFS would issue ~29 unnecessary probes exploring b=1 branches at each depth level. With early exit, only ~2 probes needed.

tests.name: deterministic_n400_spread
tests.description: Deterministic max-N test with spread elements: N=400 elements at positions i*2^21 mod (2^30) for i=0..399, ensuring elements spread across the full 30-bit space. Validates trie branching at high bits with known expected answer.

tests.name: medium_deterministic_n20
tests.description: Medium deterministic test with N=20 explicitly listed elements spanning various bit depths; provides judge-independent verification with explicit expected_answer.

tests.name: medium_deterministic_n50
tests.description: Medium deterministic test with N=50 elements covering all bit positions; explicit expected_answer for judge-independent verification.

tests.name: pitfall3_mask_offbyone
tests.description: Validates pitfall 3 (off-by-one mask): A = {2^29, 2^29+1} differ only in bit 0. Incorrect mask at depth 29 would miscompute the probe and miss one element.

tests.name: pitfall1_xor_recovery
tests.description: Validates pitfall 1 (must XOR back): A = {42}. Any query X != 0 returns res != 42, so solvers must compute 42 = res XOR X rather than using res directly.

tests.name: pitfall2_zero_and_seven
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 2 (bitwise NOT masking): A = {0, 7}. Element 0 requires probing with complement of all-zero prefix. A solver using unmasked NOT(0)=-1 would send invalid query.

tests.name: pitfall4_early_exit_two_elements
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 4 (early-exit efficiency): A = {0, 1}. Both elements cluster in low bits. Without early exit after finding both, solver wastes ~29 queries probing empty high-bit branches.

tests.name: pitfall1_xor_recovery_nonzero_query
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 1 (must XOR response with X): A = {42}. Query X=10 returns 32. Naive solver inserting 32 instead of 32 XOR 10 = 42 gets wrong answer.

tests.name: pitfall3_mask_boundary_depth29
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 3 (mask off-by-one at depth 29): A = {536870912, 536870913}. Both share bit 29=1, differ only at bit 0. Incorrect mask at depth 29 misses the split.

tests.name: dense_low_0_to_15
tests.description: Dense deterministic low-range test: A = {0,1,...,15}. All 4-bit combinations, complete sub-trie at low bits.

tests.name: three_identical_high_bits
tests.description: Three elements sharing top 28 bits, differing only in bits 1-0: A = {1073741820, 1073741821, 1073741823}. Tests deep Trie branching near the leaf level.

tests.name: early_exit_narrow_cluster
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 4 (early-exit check inside DFS loop): N=2 elements differ only in bit 0, sharing 29 upper bits. Without early exit after finding both, the DFS would waste ~29 extra queries exploring empty sibling branches at each depth.

tests.name: early_exit_high_cluster
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 4 (early-exit) with high-value elements: N=2 elements {2^30-2, 2^30-1} share 29 upper bits (all ones). Without inner early-exit, DFS wastes queries on empty lower branches after finding both elements.

tests.name: xor_recovery_validation
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 1 (must compute y = Q(X) XOR X, not use Q(X) directly): single element A={42}. Any query recovers the element only if the XOR-back step is performed.

tests.name: bitwise_not_range_validation
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 2 (bitwise NOT must be masked to valid range): A={0, 7}, where prefix=0 requires NOT(0) which is -1 in many languages if not masked.

tests.name: dense_low_n10
tests.description: Validates edge case: dense consecutive elements in a narrow sub-trie. A={0,1,...,9}. Tests that confirmed Trie branches skip queries correctly.

tests.name: same_high_prefix_n5
tests.description: Validates edge case: all elements share the same high prefix (bits 29..10 all ones), differing only in lower 10 bits. Tests mask boundary with deep shared prefix.

tests.name: alternating_bits_pair
tests.description: Validates complement pair edge case: A={0x2AAAAAAA, 0x15555555} (alternating bit patterns). These are 30-bit complements, testing full Trie branching at every depth.

tests.name: flush_deadlock_singleton
tests.description: Validates Pitfall 5 (flush requirement): singleton A={999999999}. Even a single query must be flushed for the interaction to proceed.

tests.name: adversarial_chain_trie_v2
tests.description: Adversarial: 31 chain elements (42 XOR 2^k for k=0..29, plus 42 itself) form a depth-30 chain. 370 filler elements in [2^29, 2^29+370) pad to N=400. Random-query approaches cannot find element 42.
